title: [godot4.6.beta3] Memory leak in KinematicCollision3D generated by CharacterBody3D's move_and_collide method
body: ### Tested versions Godot Engine v4.6.beta3.official.76dda5c6c ### System information windows10 forward+ ### Issue description The KinematicCollision3D object containing collision information returned by the move_and_collide method of CharacterBody3D suffers from a memory leak issue. Even after setting velocity to 0, disabling the collision_mask, and removing the node from the scene tree, the KinematicCollision3D object is still not released. It only gets freed when the CharacterBody3D instance that called move_and_collide is completely queue_free'd. This causes memory leaks when using object pooling. ### Steps to reproduce Reproduction code: Bullet.gd ```gdscript extend CharacterBody3D var end = false var move_speed = 8 var ENTITY_MASK = 16 func _physics_process(delta) : if end: destroy() return var direction: Vector3 = global_transform.basis.z * -1 direction = direction.normalized() var collid_info: KinematicCollision3D = move_and_collide(direction * delta * move_speed, false, 0.01) if collid_info != null and onexplode(collid_info): OnEnd() func onexplode(collid_info: KinematicCollision3D=null) -> bool: var collider = collid_info.get_collider() if collider.collision_layer & ENTITY_MASK: OnDamage(collider) return true return true func OnEnd() -> void: end = true set_collision_mask(0) func destroy() -> void: velocity = Vector3.ZERO for nodeob in get_collision_exceptions(): remove_collision_exception_with(nodeob) ObjectPool.FactoryRecycle(self) ``` -------------------------------------------------------- ObjectPool.gd ```gdscript extend Node static var pool = [] static func FactoryRecycle(_revive_ob) -> void: _revive_ob.set_physics_process(false) _revive_ob.set_process(false) if _revive_ob.get_parent() != null: _revive_ob.get_parent().remove_child(_revive_ob) pool.append(_revive_ob) static func CleanupOldPooledObjects() -> void: for _revive_ob in pool: if _revive_ob.get_parent() != null: _revive_ob.get_parent().remove_child(_revive_ob) _revive_ob.queue_free() ``` ---------------------------------------------- 213 ObjectDBProfile.image The KinematicCollision3D object marked as 213 in the screenshot is the residual data. (I have verified through debugging that all bullet instances have been added to the object pool, and I have stopped all attack actions. Moreover, once the CleanupOldPooledObjects function of the object pool is executed to free all bullet instances in the pool, these KinematicCollision3D objects are also released along with them. As you can see from the code, there are no references to KinematicCollision3D objects anywhere.) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)
